newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New engine overhaul centre takes over in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: New engine overhaul centre takes over in Hong Kong.

text.p: A new joint venture between Rolls Royce and Hong Kong Aircraft Engineering (HAECO) to overhaul aircraft engines in the territory is now open for business.
Details of new contracts are expected to be announced within days, said Tom Begley, the director and general manager of the new company, Hong Kong Aero Engine Services Limited (HAESL).

HAESL has taken over engine overhaul and testing previously carried out by sister company HAECO, which is also part of the Swire Group a major shareholder of Cathay Pacific Airways Limited and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair). Both airlines are Rolls Royce customers.

"HAECO is now out of the engine business and we have been busy transferring existing engine overhaul contracts with HAECO. We should be able to announce details of at least three contracts which are waiting to be signed within a few days," Begley said.

The new company's centrepiece is the biggest engine test cell in Asia capable of handling 130,000 lbs of thrust. A module change and repair site make up the rest of HAESL's $120 million development at Tseung Kwan O which is expected to open next month following a fire department inspection visit next week and occupancy approval by the Hong Kong government, Begley told Reuters in an interview.

"With a fair wind we should be operating in our new test cell, which is visually quite spectacular, from the first week in March. The equipment is installed and ready to switch on," Begley said. The test centre's formal opening is not expected to be until mid-July.

One hundred and fifty Rolls Royce RB211-524 and Trent engines, which power Cathay's fleet of Boeing 747s, Boeing 777 and Airbus A330 aircraft, are due to be overhauled and tested this year by HAESL's 500 workforce. Engines due for overhaul will be taken off wing and transported by low loader truck to the new centre near Clearwater Bay instead of at HAECO's workshops at Kai Tak airport which are due to close down next year when Hong Kong's new airport opens at Chek Lap Kok.
HAESL has also begun a marketing campaign to attract more airlines which use Rolls Royce engines to the new Hong Kong centre, Begley said.

Garuda Indonesia, Thai Airways International and Malaysia Airlines are all recent Rolls Royce customers but Begley could not confirm whether contracts with them are being sought. Singapore Airlines, another major Rolls Royce customer for its new fleet of Boeing 777s, will not be a HAESL customer because a rival engine overhaul centre is planned in Singapore, Begley confirmed.

"We are looking for new business. It doesn't take too much guesswork to see who we are talking to about major contracts but we have a bit of work to do before they can be announced," Begley added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
